title: Tomato Sauce

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: Extra virgin olive oil – 80 ml (about ⅓ cup)
San Marzano tomatoes (DOP, whole peeled) – 2 x 800g cans (or the best quality you can source)
Freshly cracked black pepper – to taste
Fresh basil leaves – 1 small bunch, tied with string (bouquet)
Pinch of sugar – optional, only if acidity is harsh
Unsalted butter – 2 tbsp (for finishing, silky texture)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Build the soffritto (foundation)
steps: In a heavy-bottomed pot, warm the olive oil over medium heat.
Sweat gently (do not brown) for 10–12 minutes until soft and sweet.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Garlic & tomato paste
steps: Add garlic, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste, and cook slowly for 2–3 minutes to caramelize—this deepens the sauce’s base.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Tomatoes
steps: Crush the San Marzano tomatoes by hand (or pass through a food mill for a smoother texture).
Add them to the pot along with their juices.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Season & infuse
steps: Add salt, pepper, basil bouquet, thyme, and bay leaf.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Slow reduction
steps: Simmer uncovered over low heat for 60–90 minutes, stirring occasionally.
The sauce should thicken, concentrate, and lose any raw tomato taste.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Finish
steps: Remove herb stems and bay leaf.
For a luxurious texture, swirl in 2 tbsp of butter just before serving.

chefTips: Tomatoes matter: Always use San Marzano DOP or high-quality canned plum tomatoes. They define the depth and balance of true Italian sauces.
Texture choice: For a rustic feel, leave it chunky. For fine dining, pass the sauce through a chinois or blend until silky.
No shortcuts: Resist adding oregano, heavy spices, or sugar (except a tiny pinch if tomatoes are overly acidic). True Italian sauces are about purity and restraint.
